Definition: Seir, a mountain of Idumaea and its aboriginal occupants, also one in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Seir is a mountain, a man, and a people, all in one name. The sons of Seir are named in the genealogy of the Horites, and the children of mount Seir came against Judah with Ammon and Moab — and when Judah began to sing and to praise, the LORD set ambushments against them, and they were smitten.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Seir stands as a warning and a wonder together: the mountain people who opposed Judah were destroyed, and they were destroyed while God's people sang.
